actions.action: Monitor new growth for a couple of weeks after bringing the tree home
Prune off brown or unsightly growth
Water thoroughly when the top of the soil feels somewhat dry, without letting it sit in water
Make sure the pot has drainage holes
If a trunk rots and feels squishy, pluck it out
Place in bright light a couple of feet back from a south window, near other plants for humidity
Occasionally fertilize with Miracle-Gro indoor plant food during the growing season
Shake the top of the tree occasionally to strengthen trunks
Rotate the plant for even light and growth
Braid young pliable branches and tie them off with a twist tie
Prune lower leaves as the braid grows
Check for a tie or rubber band at the base of the trunks and remove it

verdict.reason: The answer is mostly a general care guide; it only mentions removing a tie at the base, which lets the bound trunks separate, as a buried side tip rather than identifying the tangled multiple trees as the cause, and none of its advice is likely to harm the plant.
